A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRIDGE study. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v2's Appendices A–E. v1 ends with references and has no appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments on three LLMs, including benchmark accuracy, training dynamics, epoch comparisons and computational costs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds out-of-domain evaluation and LoRA sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The base-model/LoRA architecture, bilevel optimization, penalty relaxation and update algorithms remain unchanged. Equation 3 changes the incorrect-answer reward to 0, but v1's experimental settings already specify 0; this establishes a formulation correction, not a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation of math-trained Qwen3-8B on LiveCodeBench v5 and GPQA, extending coverage to coding and graduate-level question answering. The mathematical training data and five original math benchmarks remain. DeepSeekMath-103k becoming DeepMath-103k corrects the name of the same cited dataset.

E2.justification: The existing math comparisons retain their baselines. The new Qwen3-8B OOD comparison includes an Instruct comparator alongside Base, RL-zero and Cold-start; the original Qwen3 comparison did not include Instruct. SFT and Naive Alternating are absent from this new comparison. CHORD and LUFFY are discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces controlled LoRA variations: rank/alpha settings of 32/16 and 16/32, with other training settings fixed. The stated default remains 16/16. Existing batch sizes, learning rate, rollout budgets, decoding settings, metrics and hardware are retained in Appendix B.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of transfer from mathematical training to two non-math domains and a controlled investigation of LoRA hyperparameter sensitivity. These broaden the analysis beyond v1's training dynamics, epoch comparisons and alternating-method ablation. The existing epoch analysis is retained and partly moved to Appendix C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice; the mean-reward plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports BRIDGE scores of 34.55 on LiveCodeBench and 42.93 on GPQA, highest among its listed comparators. Table 7 reports averages of 49.9 and 49.5 under different LoRA settings. In retained Table 3, Naive Alternating's AIME24/AMC23 entries change from 65.0/13.3 to 13.3/65.0. Other original numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 3 changes the formally defined incorrect-answer reward from -1 to 0, aligning it with v1's implementation description. The bilevel definitions, penalty derivation, Danskin-based reasoning and remaining equations are unchanged. No new theoretical proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about bilevel SFT–RL cooperation, accuracy and efficiency. The abstract foregrounds forgetting and adds numerical efficiency gains already reported in v1, without changing the underlying contribution claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of cross-domain transfer and insensitivity to LoRA choices. It removes v1's entire limitations discussion concerning noisy distilled traces, reasoning robustness and restricted model/domain coverage. The math-results discussion also shifts emphasis from possible SFT overfitting toward constrained RL exploration.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly assigns LIMR to Qwen2.5-3B and MATH to the other models, and documents the LoRA variations. Most implementation details merely move to Appendix B. The prospective code-release URL and explicit statement excluding format-based rewards are removed; this does not establish any change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive contrasts with CHORD's weighted objective mixing and LUFFY's off-policy guidance, plus citations for the OOD benchmarks. Curriculum-learning and limitations-related citations are removed. The original RL and bilevel-optimization review, including its novelty positioning, survives in Appendix E.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: implementation details, epoch discussion and the original related-work review move into appendices. Baseline descriptions are condensed, the abstract/introduction and results narrative are revised, and an LLM-use disclosure is added. The limitations section is removed.

P2.justification: All three figure images are retained, but relocated and renumbered, notably moving training dynamics onto the first page. Two tables are added, the epoch table is compressed beside the OOD table, and table captions move above the displays. Typography, running headers and page composition change throughout.

improvement.justification: The new OOD results provide useful evidence beyond v1's math-only evaluation, while the CHORD/LUFFY discussion better contextualizes BRIDGE and Equation 3 becomes internally consistent with the reported reward implementation. These are meaningful but limited gains. The sensitivity study covers only two LoRA variations, and removing the specific limitations discussion and code-release pointer weakens transparency.
